title: Electromagnetism, thermal physics and quantum background
scope: Non-gravitational background physics the books assume and briefly re-teach, in three-vector and elementary form: electric charge and its local conservation, the Lorentz force, Maxwell equations and Gauss law, scalar and vector potentials with gauge freedom and the Coulomb gauge, electromagnetic waves, plane waves and polarization, retarded potentials, and field energy density, Poynting flux and Maxwell stress; the laws of thermodynamics and free energy, black-body radiation, the Stefan-Boltzmann law and photon-gas statistics; and elementary quantum and particle physics (Planck and de Broglie relations, photons and the photoelectric effect, uncertainty relations, the Pauli principle, Fermi momentum and degenerate Fermi gases, antiparticles, virtual particles, isospin and the Standard Model as vocabulary). Covariant tensor and forms versions of Maxwell theory, relativistic fluid thermodynamics, stellar degeneracy pressure and black-hole thermodynamics are owned by later domains.

concepts.title: Electric charge
concepts.summary: Electric charge is the conserved scalar property of a particle that fixes how strongly it couples to the electromagnetic field; in a relativistic action it is the constant multiplying the line integral of the four-potential along the world line.

concepts.title: Charge conservation
concepts.summary: Charge is conserved locally: the charge density can change in a region only by current flowing through its boundary, expressed as the continuity equation d(rho)/dt + div j = 0 (a vanishing four-divergence of the current). Integrating the density over a volume gives the total charge, whose change equals the net outward flux.
concepts.notes: Local conservation is stronger than global conservation: a law that only fixed total charge would allow charge to vanish here and reappear far away, which relativity forbids. In Maxwell theory it follows from the sourced equations (antisymmetry of F). The generic four-current object is owned by matter-and-stress-energy.

concepts.title: Lorentz force law
aliases: equation of motion of a charge
concepts.summary: A charge q moving with velocity v in fields E and B feels the force q(E + v x B); covariantly, the rate of change of its four-momentum with proper time is q times the Faraday tensor contracted with its four-velocity, so in curved spacetime it measures the departure from geodesic motion.
concepts.notes: GA ch42 derives the covariant form from an action and quotes the three-vector form as its limit; GA ch48 recovers the same law from five-dimensional free motion (Kaluza-Klein).

concepts.title: Cyclotron motion
aliases: helical motion in a magnetic field
concepts.summary: A charged particle in a uniform magnetic field circles the field direction at a fixed angular rate while moving uniformly along it, so its path is a helix.

names: helical motion in a magnetic field

merged_from: helical motion in a magnetic field

concepts.title: Maxwell equations
concepts.summary: The four field equations of electromagnetism: div E = rho and curl B - dE/dt = j contain the sources, while div B = 0 and curl E + dB/dt = 0 do not and become identities once the fields are written in terms of potentials.
concepts.notes: Books use natural Heaviside-Lorentz units with c = 1 (no 4 pi in the equations). The tensor form, curved-spacetime form (matter-and-stress-energy) and forms version dF = 0, d*F = *J (differential-forms-and-frames) are owned elsewhere; this concept is the three-vector statement and its source/source-free split.

concepts.title: Gauss law
aliases: total charge as a surface integral
concepts.summary: Integrating div E = rho over a region and applying the divergence theorem shows that the enclosed charge equals the electric flux through the bounding surface; total charge of an isolated system is the flux through a sphere at infinity.
concepts.notes: DIV ch20 uses the curved-spacetime version (flux of F through a 2-surface on a spacelike hypersurface) as the template for defining the mass of a gravitating system.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic potentials
aliases: E and B in terms of A
concepts.summary: The fields can be derived from a scalar potential V and a vector potential A as E = -grad V - dA/dt and B = curl A; together (V, A) form the components of the four-potential, and this form makes the source-free Maxwell equations automatic.

names: electric and magnetic fields from potentials

merged_from: electric and magnetic fields from potentials

concepts.title: Electromagnetic gauge transformation
concepts.summary: Adding the gradient of an arbitrary scalar function to the four-potential, A_mu -> A_mu - d_mu chi, leaves E, B and the Maxwell equations unchanged; this redundancy lets one impose a convenient gauge condition, and it is the template for gauge freedom in linearized gravity.
concepts.notes: The generic "gauge transformation" cluster is owned by gravitational-waves; only its electromagnetic mentions (GA ch42, DIV ch12) are recorded here. The Lorenz gauge condition d_mu A^mu = 0 is registered by gravitational-waves; the reinterpretation as a local U(1) phase symmetry belongs to action-principles-and-field-theory.

concepts.title: Coulomb gauge
concepts.summary: The gauge condition div A = 0; in a source-free region it can be combined with A_0 = 0 (the radiation gauge), which leaves only transverse components of the potential.
concepts.notes: GA reaches it from Lorenz gauge using residual gauge freedom; it is the model for the transverse-traceless gauge of gravitational waves.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic wave equation
aliases: wave equations for E and B
concepts.summary: In Lorenz gauge and away from sources each component of the four-potential, and hence of E and B, obeys the wave equation, so electromagnetic disturbances travel at the speed of light.
concepts.notes: With sources the Lorenz-gauge equation reads box A^mu = -J^mu; the matching of this to the displacement current was Maxwell's route to light as an electromagnetic wave.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic plane wave
concepts.summary: A vacuum solution A = epsilon exp(i k.x) with null wave vector; the gauge conditions force the polarization vector to be perpendicular to the propagation direction, leaving exactly two independent transverse polarizations.
concepts.notes: GA ch47 recovers the count of two physical photon polarizations from the propagating part of an exchange amplitude, as a rehearsal for the two graviton polarizations.

concepts.title: Retarded potential
concepts.summary: The causal solution of the sourced wave equation: the potential at (t, x) is an integral of the source divided by distance, with each source element evaluated at the retarded time t - |x - x'|/c when a light-speed signal must have left it.
concepts.notes: GA ch45 carries the electromagnetic result over to linearized gravity by replacing J with 16 pi G T. Retarded time in the sense of a null coordinate in black-hole spacetimes (DIV ch17) belongs to black-holes; the gravitational retarded solution is owned by gravitational-waves.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic energy density
concepts.summary: Electric and magnetic fields store energy per unit volume proportional to E^2 + B^2 ((E^2 + B^2)/2 in Heaviside-Lorentz units, (E^2 + B^2)/8 pi in Gaussian units); it is the time-time component of the Maxwell stress-energy tensor.

concepts.title: Poynting vector
concepts.summary: The vector E x B (times a unit-dependent constant) gives the rate at which field energy flows through unit area; with c = 1 it also equals the momentum density of the field, the T^0i components of the stress-energy tensor.

concepts.title: Maxwell stress tensor
concepts.summary: The purely spatial block of the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor, giving the flux of field momentum: the pressures and shears that fields exert across surfaces.

concepts.title: Fermat principle
concepts.summary: Light travels between two points along a path whose travel time is stationary (usually a minimum) with respect to small variations of the path.
concepts.notes: GA ch02 uses it to motivate an action proportional to proper time.

concepts.title: First law of thermodynamics
concepts.summary: Energy conservation for a thermodynamic system: the change in internal energy equals heat absorbed minus work done, dU = T dS - p dV for reversible changes.
concepts.notes: GA applies it to a comoving cosmic volume (ch17) and uses it as the template for black-hole thermodynamics (ch28); the fluid-element and relativistic versions are owned by matter-and-stress-energy.

concepts.title: Second law of thermodynamics
concepts.summary: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases; for a relativistic fluid element this means the entropy per baryon cannot decrease along its world line.

concepts.title: Helmholtz free energy
concepts.summary: At fixed temperature a system in equilibrium minimizes F = U - TS, which balances the tendency toward low energy against the tendency toward high entropy.
concepts.notes: GA ch41 uses it as the starting point for Landau theory of phase transitions and spontaneous symmetry breaking.

concepts.title: Planck relation
concepts.summary: A quantum of electromagnetic radiation with frequency nu carries energy E = h nu (equivalently hbar omega).
concepts.notes: DIV ch04 combines it with E = pc for photon momentum and argues it is consistent with the relativistic Doppler effect; SCH ch02 uses it to translate photon four-momentum into frequency.

concepts.title: Photoelectric effect
concepts.summary: Light, especially ultraviolet, ejects electrons from a metal; Einstein explained it by the absorption of individual quanta of energy h nu, making it key early evidence for light quanta.

concepts.title: Wave-particle duality
concepts.summary: Light behaves as a wave in interference and diffraction but as a stream of particles when it exchanges energy with matter, as in the photoelectric effect.

concepts.title: Photon
concepts.summary: The quantum of the electromagnetic field: a particle moving at c with zero rest mass, energy h nu and momentum h nu/c along its direction of travel.
concepts.notes: DIV ch04 obtains zero rest mass by setting u = c in the relativistic mass formula and stresses that no inertial observer can bring a photon to rest. Photon four-momentum and Doppler shifts are owned by special-relativity.

concepts.title: de Broglie relation
concepts.summary: Every particle has an associated wave whose wave vector is proportional to momentum, p = hbar k with |k| = 2 pi/lambda; relativistically the four-momentum is hbar times the wave four-vector.

concepts.title: Heisenberg uncertainty principle
concepts.summary: Position and momentum cannot both be sharp: their spreads obey Delta x Delta p of order hbar or more, so a particle confined to a volume has a minimum momentum spread.
concepts.notes: Not a mechanical candidate cluster; added because SCH ch10 builds phase-space cells from it and SCH ch11 uses it to estimate the Hawking energy.

concepts.title: Energy-time uncertainty relation
concepts.summary: Heuristically Delta E Delta t ~ hbar: a state that lasts only a time Delta t has an energy uncertain by about hbar/Delta t, which bounds how long an energy-violating fluctuation can persist.
concepts.notes: GA ch28 uses it for vacuum pair lifetimes and to estimate the energy of a photon near a horizon.

concepts.title: Black-body spectrum
concepts.summary: Radiation in thermal equilibrium at temperature T has spectral energy density proportional to nu^3/(exp(h nu/k_B T) - 1); the peak lies near h nu = 2.82 k_B T and the mean photon energy is about 2.7 k_B T.

concepts.title: Stefan-Boltzmann law
concepts.summary: Integrating the black-body spectrum gives a radiation energy density a T^4 and an emitted power per unit area sigma T^4, so a black body of area A radiates power proportional to A T^4.
concepts.notes: DIV ch26 applies the energy-density form to the CMB today; GA ch28 applies the luminosity form with A = 16 pi M^2 to black-hole evaporation.

concepts.title: Photon gas partition function
concepts.summary: Statistical mechanics of an ultra-relativistic gas: a single-particle partition function proportional to V T^3 gives mean energy 3 k_B T per particle and pressure equal to one third of the energy density.

concepts.title: Pauli exclusion principle
aliases: Pauli exclusion principle and phase-space cells
counting quantum states in momentum space
concepts.summary: No two identical fermions can occupy the same quantum state; since each momentum-space cell of volume h^3/V is one state, it holds at most two spin-1/2 fermions.

names: Pauli exclusion principle and phase-space cells

merged_from: Pauli exclusion principle and phase-space cells
concepts.notes: SCH ch10 counts states by dividing momentum space into cells, the step that forces a cold dense gas into high-momentum states.

concepts.title: Fermi momentum
concepts.summary: When N fermions fill the lowest momentum states in volume V, the largest occupied momentum p_F satisfies n = 8 pi p_F^3/(3 h^3) for spin-1/2 particles, so it depends only on number density and not on particle mass.

concepts.title: Degenerate Fermi gas
concepts.summary: A fermion gas so dense or cold that every momentum state up to the Fermi momentum is filled; its energy density and pressure are set by density alone and stay large even at zero temperature.
concepts.notes: The resulting degeneracy pressure and its stellar applications belong to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars.

concepts.title: Antiparticle
concepts.summary: Every observed particle and antiparticle has positive energy; the negative-energy root of the relativistic dispersion relation is reinterpreted as an antiparticle with positive energy and reversed momentum, equivalently a negative-energy state running backward in time.
concepts.notes: GA ch28 corrects the common claim that antiparticles carry negative energy.

concepts.title: Virtual particle
concepts.summary: An intermediate quantum whose four-momentum does not satisfy the free mass-shell condition p.p = -m^2; the energy-time uncertainty relation lets it exist only briefly, so it appears only inside processes and sets the range of the force it carries.

concepts.title: Isospin
concepts.summary: An internal quantum number that treats related particles such as the proton and neutron as two states of one object, with a symmetry rotating one identity into the other at each point.
concepts.notes: GA ch44 mentions it as an example of an internal space (fibre) beyond a complex phase.

concepts.title: Standard Model of particle physics
concepts.summary: The quantum gauge field theory with symmetry group SU(3) x SU(2) x U(1) that describes quarks, leptons, the Higgs field and the strong, weak and electromagnetic interactions; gravity is not included.

concepts.title: Many-worlds interpretation
concepts.summary: An interpretation of quantum mechanics in which every measurement-like interaction splits the universe into non-interacting branches, one for each possible outcome.
concepts.notes: DIV ch26 mentions it only as one route to many universes in anthropic arguments.

out_of_scope_candidates.name: conformal invariance of electromagnetism
